propositions: Operator-attested evidence contract currently demands provenance of the attestation event (change id, vote, timestamp) but not provenance of the measurement itself (environment, principal, privilege level), allowing attestations from wrong environments or under broader privilege to pass.

Two known escape cases succeeded: bedrock measurements from account 579718921998/us-east-2 attested for work targeting 896586841071/us-east-1, and live bedrock:Converse calls under bedrock:* privilege offered as validation of a scoped bedrock:InvokeModel grant that would have failed in production.

The mechanism must force measurement context (environment, principal, privilege_posture, instrument) into the attestation record as text, then let repo-grounded checkers find contradictions between declared values and actual IaC anchors.

A new deterministic check must validate presence and shape of four required provenance fields (environment, principal, privilege_posture with enum values, instrument with enum values) and reject placeholder values, without judging correctness; an AGENT-tier criterion must then judge declarations against repo facts and authorization semantics.

The instrument field must be independently checked for authorization claims: simulation or static-analysis instruments are insufficient evidence even when privilege_posture is production-equivalent, because simulators cannot discover API runtime behavior that live calls can.
